I believe this section in the README should point to section E1.1 instead of E2.1.
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/1fff04023abdd628a288c8ae838b9269cc98e5e1/README.md?plain=1#L76-L86

Here are the potentially relevant code snippets: ### Code Snippet 0: README.md 1 # AXI SystemVerilog Modules for High-Performance On-Chip Communication 2 [![CI status](https://akurth.net/usrv/ig/shields/pipeline/akurth/axi/master.svg)](https://iis-git.ee.ethz.ch/akurth/axi/commits/master) 3 [![GitHub tag (latest SemVer)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/pulp-platform/axi?color=blue&label=current&sort=semver)](CHANGELOG.md) 4 [![SHL-0.51 license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-SHL--0.51-green)](LICENSE) 5 6 This repository provides modules to build on-chip communication networks adhering to the [AXI4 or AXI4-Lite standards](https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ihi0022/hc). For high-performance communication, we implement AXI4[+ATOPs from AXI5](#atomic-operations). For lightweight communication, we implement AXI4-Lite. We aim to provide a complete end-to-end communication platform, including endpoints such as DMA engines and on-chip memory controllers. 7 8 Our **design goals** are: 9 - **Topology Independence**: We provide elementary building blocks such as protocol [multiplexers](src/axi_mux.sv) and [demultiplexers](src/axi_demux.sv) that allow users to implement any network topology. We also provide commonly used interconnecting components such as a [crossbar](src/axi_xbar.sv). 10 - **Modularity**: We favor design by composition over design by configuration where possible. We strive to apply the *Unix philosophy* to hardware: make each module do one thing well. This means you will more often instantiate our modules back-to-back than change a parameter value to build more specialized networks. 11 - **Fit for Heterogeneous Networks**: Our modules are parametrizable in terms of data width and transaction concurrency. This allows to create optimized networks for a wide range of performance (e.g., bandwidth, concurrency, timing), power, and area requirements. We provide modules such as [data width converters](src/axi_dw_converter.sv) and [ID width converters](src/axi_iw_converter.sv) that allow to join subnetworks with different properties, creating heterogeneous on-chip networks. 12 - **Full AXI Standard Compliance**. 13 - **Compatibility** with a [wide range of (recent versions of) EDA tools](#which-eda-tools-are-supported) and implementation in standardized synthesizable SystemVerilog. 14 15 The **design and microarchitecture** of the modules in this repository is described in [**this paper**](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9522037) ([preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.05334)). If you use our work in your research, please cite it. ### Code Snippet 1: doc/README.md 1 # Documentation of AXI Modules 2 3 This folder contains the documentation of the following modules: 4 5 - [AXI Crossbar (`axi_xbar`)](axi_xbar.md) 6 - [AXI Demultiplexer (`axi_demux`)](axi_demux.md) 7 - [AXI Multiplexer (`axi_mux`)](axi_mux.md) 8 - [AXI4-Lite Mailbox (`axi_lite_mailbox`)](axi_lite_mailbox.md) 9 10 11 ## Relevant Specifications 12 13 We adhere to the *AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification, Issue F.b*, abbreviated as *AXI Spec* in these documents. 14 15 ### Code Snippet 2: README.md 66 | [`axi_lite_driver`](src/axi_test.sv) | Low-level driver for AXI4-Lite that can send and receive individual beats on any channel. | 67 | [`axi_lite_rand_master`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4-Lite master component that issues random transactions within user-defined constraints. | 68 | [`axi_lite_rand_slave`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4-Lite slave component that responds to transactions with constrainable random delays and data. | 69 | [`axi_rand_master`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4(+ATOPs) master component that issues random transactions within user-defined constraints. | 70 | [`axi_rand_slave`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4(+ATOPs) slave component that responds to transactions with constrainable random delays and data. | 71 | [`axi_scoreboard`](src/axi_test.sv) | Scoreboard that models a memory that only gets changed by the monitored AXI4(+ATOPs) port. | 72 | [`axi_sim_mem`](src/axi_sim_mem.sv) | Infinite memory with AXI4 slave port. | 73 74 75 76 ## Atomic Operations 77 78 AXI4+ATOPs means the full AXI4 specification plus atomic operations (ATOPs) as defined in Section E1.1 of the AMBA5 specification. This has the following implications for modules that do not implement ATOPs and systems that include such modules: 79 80 - Masters that do not issue ATOPs must set `aw_atop` to `'0`. 81 - Slaves that do not support ATOPs must specify this in their interface documentation and can ignore the `aw_atop` signal. 82 - System designers are responsible for ensuring that 83 1. slaves that do not support ATOPs are behind an [`axi_atop_filter`](src/axi_atop_filter.sv) if any master could issue an ATOP to such slaves and 84 2. the `aw_atop` signal is well-defined at the input of any (non-AXI4-Lite) module in this repository. 85 ### Code Snippet 3: README.md 68 | [`axi_lite_rand_slave`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4-Lite slave component that responds to transactions with constrainable random delays and data. | 69 | [`axi_rand_master`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4(+ATOPs) master component that issues random transactions within user-defined constraints. | 70 | [`axi_rand_slave`](src/axi_test.sv) | AXI4(+ATOPs) slave component that responds to transactions with constrainable random delays and data. | 71 | [`axi_scoreboard`](src/axi_test.sv) | Scoreboard that models a memory that only gets changed by the monitored AXI4(+ATOPs) port. | 72 | [`axi_sim_mem`](src/axi_sim_mem.sv) | Infinite memory with AXI4 slave port. | 73 74 75 76 ## Atomic Operations 77 78 AXI4+ATOPs means the full AXI4 specification plus atomic operations (ATOPs) as defined in Section E1.1 of the AMBA5 specification. This has the following implications for modules that do not implement ATOPs and systems that include such modules: 79 80 - Masters that do not issue ATOPs must set `aw_atop` to `'0`. 81 - Slaves that do not support ATOPs must specify this in their interface documentation and can ignore the `aw_atop` signal. 82 - System designers are responsible for ensuring that 83 1. slaves that do not support ATOPs are behind an [`axi_atop_filter`](src/axi_atop_filter.sv) if any master could issue an ATOP to such slaves and 84 2. the `aw_atop` signal is well-defined at the input of any (non-AXI4-Lite) module in this repository. 85 86 Masters and slaves that do support ATOPs must adhere to Section E1.1 of the AMBA5 specification. 87 ### Code Snippet 4: README.md 76 ## Atomic Operations 77 78 AXI4+ATOPs means the full AXI4 specification plus atomic operations (ATOPs) as defined in Section E1.1 of the AMBA5 specification. This has the following implications for modules that do not implement ATOPs and systems that include such modules: 79 80 - Masters that do not issue ATOPs must set `aw_atop` to `'0`. 81 - Slaves that do not support ATOPs must specify this in their interface documentation and can ignore the `aw_atop` signal. 82 - System designers are responsible for ensuring that 83 1. slaves that do not support ATOPs are behind an [`axi_atop_filter`](src/axi_atop_filter.sv) if any master could issue an ATOP to such slaves and 84 2. the `aw_atop` signal is well-defined at the input of any (non-AXI4-Lite) module in this repository. 85 86 Masters and slaves that do support ATOPs must adhere to Section E1.1 of the AMBA5 specification. 87 88 89 ## Which EDA Tools Are Supported? 90 91 Our code is written in standard SystemVerilog ([IEEE 1800-2012][], to be precise), so the more important question is: Which subset of SystemVerilog does your EDA tool support? 92 93 We aim to be compatible with a wide range of EDA tools. For this reason, we strive to use as simple language constructs as possible, especially for our synthesizable modules. We encourage contributions that further simplify our code to make it compatible with even more EDA tools. We also welcome contributions that work around problems that specific EDA tools may have with our code, as long as: 94 - the EDA tool is reasonably widely used, 95 - recent versions of the EDA tool are affected,

<analysis>
The reported issue is a documentation pointer error in the README’s ATOP/AXI5 wording. The user believes the spec reference should point to Section E1.1 instead of E2.1.

From the provided snippets, the relevant content is concentrated in the top-level `README.md`, specifically the “Atomic Operations” section. The core line already shown in snippets 2–4 states that ATOPs are defined in Section E1.1, so the issue description likely refers to an older or alternate line in the same section that may still mention E2.1 in the repository version referenced by the issue link. That means the main area to inspect is the README’s ATOP explanation and any nearby lines referencing the AMBA5 specification.

Related locations to inspect include:
- The “Atomic Operations” section in `README.md` around lines 76–86, where all AXI5/ATOP references are described.
- Any adjacent text in the same section that mentions specification sections, because a mismatch could exist in a neighboring sentence or in another mirrored statement.
- `doc/README.md` only as contextual documentation, since it defines the spec baseline as AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification Issue F.b, but it does not mention E1.1/E2.1. It is useful to inspect for consistency, though no direct issue is visible in the snippet.
- There are no class or method-based code locations here; this appears to be pure documentation content.

Because the task is to identify all related locations requiring inspection or modification, the only concrete edit location visible in the snippets is the README’s Atomic Operations block. If the repository has other documentation files or duplicated explanation blocks for ATOPs, they should be checked for the same section reference inconsistency, but among the provided snippets only `README.md` contains the relevant text.
